Serve the current session over Quack

Source: R/quack.R
quack_serve.Rd

Starts a Quack server in the current DuckDB instance. Everything attached to the session, including a DuckLake attached with attach_ducklake(), becomes reachable by other DuckDB clients over the quack: protocol. The server runs in the background of the DuckDB instance, so the R session stays usable.

Usage

quack_serve(
  uri = "quack:localhost",
  token = NULL,
  allow_other_hostname = FALSE,
  disable_ssl = FALSE,
  secret = NULL,
  create_secret_if_not_exists = FALSE,
  ssl_cert_file = NULL,
  ssl_key_file = NULL
)

Arguments

uri

Address to listen on (default "quack:localhost"). The default port is 9494.

token

Authentication token that clients must supply (at least 4 characters). If NULL, the server takes the token of the session's default Quack secret when there is one (see secret and create_secret_if_not_exists), and otherwise generates a random token, which the returned data frame carries in auth_token. A server is never open: clients always present a token.

allow_other_hostname

Accept connections addressed to a hostname other than the one in uri (default FALSE). A server reachable from other machines belongs behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy.

disable_ssl

Serve over plain HTTP instead of HTTPS (default FALSE, which leaves the choice to DuckDB: plain HTTP for a local address, HTTPS otherwise). Only appropriate on a trusted network.

secret

Optional name of an existing Quack secret whose token the server uses.

create_secret_if_not_exists

When no token is given and no default Quack secret exists, store the generated token in a persistent default secret, so later servers (and clients in this session) reuse it (default FALSE).

ssl_cert_file, ssl_key_file

Optional certificate and private key files for serving over HTTPS, such as the pair quack_generate_keys() writes. Without them DuckDB generates a self-signed certificate when it serves HTTPS.

Value

Invisibly, a data frame with one row: listen_uri, listen_url, and auth_token, the token clients must present.

See also

quack_stop(), attach_quack(), quack_generate_keys()

Other quack: attach_quack(), detach_quack(), install_quack(), quack_generate_keys(), quack_query(), quack_stop()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
attach_ducklake("trial", lake_path = "path/to/lake")
quack_serve(token = "super_secret")
# ... colleagues connect with attach_quack() ...
quack_stop()

# Let DuckDB pick the token and keep it in a secret for later servers
server <- quack_serve(create_secret_if_not_exists = TRUE)
server$auth_token
} # }
